# NumericStepper

Figma: [03p. NumericStepper](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=3895-4429) · Family: 03 Form & Input · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-01-01

A quantity stepper - − and + nudge a number by a fixed step, with min/max clamping (buttons disable at the bounds). For small integer quantities (units, guests, installments). Not the 06h process Stepper. Size × State × Direction.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/numeric-stepper/reference.png`

### NumericStepper

A compact minus / value / plus control for small integer quantities with min and max clamping. It is not the process Stepper.

Level: organism

Use when:
- Number of units or shares in a deal (small integers)
- Number of installments or similar small counts
- Value at a bound: State=AtMin or AtMax disables that button

Don't use when:
- SAR amounts: use Input Amount or Amount Stepper
- Showing steps of a multi-step flow: use Stepper
- Large or free-form numbers: use Input Amount

Accessibility: Disable the boundary button (aria-disabled) instead of ignoring taps, and announce the new value.

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

A compact control for adjusting a small number a few at a time - faster and less error-prone than typing. − decrements, + increments by the step; the value clamps between a min and max.

### Anatomy

A bordered field with − and + at the ends and the value centred.

- Decrement (−) - steps the value down; disabled at the minimum.
- Value - the current number; can be read-only or editable.
- Increment (+) - steps the value up; disabled at the maximum.

### Sizes

lg (44) · md (40) · sm (36) - matching the input scale.

### States

- Default - both buttons active.
- At-min - value at the floor; − disabled.
- At-max - value at the ceiling; + disabled.
- Disabled - whole control inert.

### Direction - LTR and RTL

In RTL the − and + swap sides - + leads (reading-start), − trails - so “increase” stays on the natural side.

### Behavior

- Step - a fixed increment (1, 5, 10…); hold to repeat is optional.
- Clamp - the value never crosses min/max; the boundary button disables (not just no-ops).
- Editable value - allow typing for large jumps; re-clamp + validate on blur.
- Debounce - coalesce rapid taps before firing onChange.

### Code examples

```typescript
<NumericStepper
  dir="rtl"
  value={qty} min={0} max={99} step={1}
  editable
  onChange={setQty}
/>
```

### Usage - Do and Don't

Do

Disable the boundary button at min/max - never let the value cross the limit.

Do

Use it for small integer quantities where a few taps beats typing.

Don’t

Don’t use a stepper for large or free-form amounts - use AmountInput (03c) instead.

### Resources

- NumericStepper - 3902:1186
- IconButton (02b) - reused pattern
- AmountInput (03c) · Input (03a)
- Stepper (06h) - the process one (different)

### Notes from the maintainer

> **Info:** Two names, two things: this is the numeric quantity stepper (Form & Input). The 06h Stepper is the multi-step process indicator. Don’t conflate them.

> **Tip:** The − / + are text glyphs here for reliability; swap in the DS minus/plus icons before publishing for pixel parity with IconButton.

> **Warning:** Always disable the boundary button (aria-disabled) rather than silently ignoring taps - users need the feedback.
